Section 2 assumes multiple non-Gaussian LiNGAM datasets with a shared causal order and possibly different coefficient matrices, and Section 3.2 jointly selects successive variables by aggregating residual-independence scores across the unpaired groups.

Equation (2), Theorem 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 identify individual linear acyclic models through shared environment components using Shared ICA, under at most one Gaussian component or a cross-individual noise-variance diversity condition.
The multi-domain linear-SEM procedure exploits shared causal structure and domain-wise heterogeneity to recover a common graph from separate domain datasets.
Its pair condition is sufficient for full linear-model identification and worst-case necessary when intervention experiments observe overlapping variable sets.
Its recursive algorithm partitions an MPDAG class into subclasses with pairwise distinct total-effect functionals.
Its maximum-cardinality-search procedure enumerates every graph-distinct DAG in a Markov equivalence class with linear delay.

The complete table also positions the previously omitted Gaussian-DAG and missing-data references.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a child oracle that discovers every previously unknown coefficient-tuple fiber exactly once with total additive subset-state and output cost, or first formalize an oracle model and then prove a matching lower bound in that model.
open_obligations.obstruction: The established fiber lemma canonicalizes inducing orders only after a tuple is known. A removed-set state can be an ideal of many different output support posets, whereas equality of completed coefficient tuples depends on all completed regression rows and is not a frozen local edge color. Testing canonicality separately for every output at every state costs a product of the subset-state and output counts, while traversing all compatible paths can remain factorial even when \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=1\). The present handle supplies neither a polynomial-time inverse-child generator nor a sufficiently formal query model from which an impossibility result could be proved.
open_obligations.attempted: The prior round examined lexicographically canonical source-to-sink paths, adjacent incomparable swaps, hashing completed paths, locally colored AND--OR quotienting, and reverse search. Lexicographic minimality depends on coefficient rows exposed only by future removals; hashing still visits factorially many paths; local colors have not been shown to form a congruence for global numerical tuples; and reverse search lacks a polynomial-time child oracle for fibers reachable only through noncanonical inducing orders. No hardness assertion is made because the oracle model remains unspecified.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), \(\text{lem:tuple-fiber-linear-extensions}\) proves that its entire compatible inducing-order fiber is the set of linear extensions of \(G_T\). Hence, once \(T\) is known, greedy topological sorting computes its lexicographically least inducing order, adjacent incomparable swaps connect its inducing orders, and \(\Gamma_\pi\succ0\) is computed in time polynomial in \(p\) and \(m\). This removes factorial duplication inside a known fiber, but it does not enumerate previously unknown fibers in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p+\operatorname{poly}(p,m)N_{\mathrm{out}})\) work or with polynomial delay.

prose_updates.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, the main completion result extends calibration subsets to an arbitrary observed view graph. A candidate common order is compatible exactly when every observed residual cross-block is diagonal and, separately for each variable, the resulting partial disturbance covariance has a positive-definite completion. For chordal view graphs this is the constructive maximal-clique test from the classical positive-definite matrix-completion theorem; a signed four-cycle shows that positive-definite edge blocks alone do not suffice for nonchordal graphs. The earlier calibration-subset certificate is the clique-plus-isolated-vertices special case. Independently, a sharp generic elbow proves that no paired block is insufficient while any one preassigned view pair identifies the full coefficient tuple off one proper algebraic exceptional set. Removed-set recursion and covariance-region inversion remain supporting results, with the latter requiring positive definiteness of the selected joint covariance. Exact-once output-sensitive quotient enumeration is not delivered and remains the explicit residual open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing multi-view LiMVAM identification results address full pairing under conditions on disturbance diversity, while Gaussian-DAG estimators target a point-identified DAG from one joint law. Neither line characterizes compatibility when cross-view covariances are observed on an arbitrary graph, where diagonal residual restrictions and positive-definite completion are distinct requirements. Existing enumeration results also do not supply the missing child oracle needed to quotient globally equal numerical coefficient tuples directly from the removed-set DAG.
project_justification.niche: For the component-aligned Gaussian subclass, a fixed candidate order determines every view-specific coefficient matrix from its marginal covariance. Each observed view edge then fixes entries of the coordinatewise disturbance covariance, so global compatibility becomes a positive-definite partial-matrix completion problem after the observable residual-diagonality test. This separates order testing, global noise feasibility, and coefficient recovery, and it retains every unpaired view marginal for coefficient estimation.
project_justification.fill: The graph-completion theorem proves necessity by restricting any full coordinatewise disturbance covariance to its observed diagonal and edge entries, and proves sufficiency by choosing one positive-definite completion for each variable and assembling independent Gaussian disturbance stacks. On chordal view graphs, the classical completion theorem reduces feasibility to positive definiteness of every maximal specified clique and supplies a constructive certificate. A nonchordal four-cycle with unit diagonals and successive edge correlations \(0.9,0.9,0.9,-0.9\) has positive-definite edge blocks but no positive-semidefinite completion, so edgewise checks alone are not valid in general. The generic calibration elbow separately proves that one observed pair is generically necessary and sufficient. The memoized removed-set DAG solves compatibility, but duplicate-free output-sensitive enumeration of all unknown tuple fibers remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor: its Section 4.6 uses edgewise cross-view correlation diversity to identify a partial order and view-specific coefficients under full pairing. The present conclusions are only for the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass and do not claim containment of the published Heurtebise class. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM motivate recursive residualization under non-Gaussianity, but they do not prove removed-set path independence or partial-view-graph covariance completion. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain pool population or domain information through ICA structure or heterogeneity rather than through selected paired cross-covariance blocks. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies overlapping experimental total-effect measurements, not residual covariance restrictions among passive views. The positive-definite completion theorem of Grone, Johnson, S\'a, and Wolkowicz (1984, Theorem 7) supplies the chordal maximal-clique criterion used by the graph specialization; the arbitrary-graph reduction and the signed four-cycle obstruction are derived for the present disturbance matrices. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects partitions graphical classes by total-effect signatures, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration enumerates graph-distinct Markov-equivalent DAGs, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration treats locally colored decomposable AND--OR graphs, and AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch requires a locally searchable parent relation. None establishes the missing quotient child oracle for global numerical modified-Cholesky tuples, so \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\) remains open. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware concern intervention-target design through separating systems, whereas the present calibration choice is passive observation of view-pair covariance blocks. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses recursive Schur updates and score gaps in a point-identifying linear SEM. GaoTaiAragam2022GaussianDAG studies point-identifying Gaussian-DAG estimation rather than partial paired-view calibration and set-valued order compatibility. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian singular-value concentration used for covariance radii, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies the general criterion-inversion comparison; neither gives the LiMVAM-specific residual and path-product moduli. MohanPearl2021MissingData studies recoverability under missingness graphs, whereas the present sourcewise-iid common-population sampling design assumes away selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN documents the MEG and MRI cohort that motivates a future diagnostic application, but it does not validate component alignment or the calibration-sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-completion characterization is population-level and remains confined to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. For nonchordal view graphs, positive definiteness of every specified edge block is only necessary; global completion must still be checked. The generic elbow is relative to a fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from its algebraic exceptional set. Covariance-region inversion requires the selected joint covariance \(\Sigma^{S,S}\succ0\) in addition to positive-definite view marginals; this premise is essential for whitening and excludes singular identical-view laws. Its Hausdorff and poset guarantees also require fixed feasibility and path-product margins. The \(2^p\)-state recursion counts exact-real arithmetic rather than bit complexity. Most importantly, \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\) remains unresolved: known-fiber canonicalization does not yield an exact-once algorithm with additive \(2^p+N_{\mathrm{out}}\) cost, and no hardness claim is justified without a formal oracle model.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The arbitrary-view-graph completion theorem, its chordal specialization, the nonchordal obstruction, the generic calibration elbow, fixed-order recovery, removed-set recursion, essential poset, and covariance-region inversion concern only the component-aligned Gaussian subclass with positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. They do not transfer automatically to unrestricted LiMVAMs or establish the assumptions used by Heurtebise et al. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed common order and gives no uniform identification margin. Finite-sample inversion additionally assumes a positive-definite selected joint covariance and sourcewise-iid common-population sampling; selection and transport are outside the model. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain prospective diagnostic applications rather than empirical validation. Exact-once output-sensitive quotient enumeration remains open.

statement_notes.gap: The new arbitrary-view-graph theorem exposes the extra global positive-definite-completion condition hidden by the calibration-subset geometry. This lemma remains the chordal special case in which the selected views form one clique and every unselected view is isolated.
statement_notes.consumer: For a selected calibration subset, an analyst obtains exactly the compatible common orders, all view-specific coefficient matrices, and a full positive-definite coordinate-noise certificate.

None establishes that global equality of completed modified-Cholesky tuples has the local compositional structure needed here, and the present handle does not define an oracle model supporting a hardness theorem.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  For each \(a\in M\), put
\[
A^{(a)}=(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}.
\]
The order restriction in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\) makes \(B^{(a)}\) strictly lower triangular after permutation by \(\pi_0\).  Hence \((B^{(a)})^p=0\), so
\[
A^{(a)}=\sum_{q=0}^{p-1}(B^{(a)})^q
\]
exists and has entries polynomial in the free structural coefficients.  Positive definiteness of each \(\Gamma_i\), also required in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\), gives \(\Gamma_i[a,a]>0\).  Therefore its covariance construction yields
\[
\Sigma_\theta^{aa}
=A^{(a)}\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i[a,a])(A^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\succ0.
\]
In particular, every predecessor principal submatrix inverted in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) is positive definite and has strictly positive determinant.

The same covariance construction shows that every entry of every \(\Sigma_\theta^{ab}\) is polynomial in the free coordinates of \(\theta\).  For each predecessor covariance matrix \(C\), the elementary adjugate identity
\[
C^{-1}=\frac{\operatorname{adj}(C)}{\det(C)}
\]
then shows that the entries of \(B_\pi^{(a)}\), and consequently those of
\[
R_\pi^{ab}=(I_p-B_\pi^{(a)})\Sigma_\theta^{ab}(I_p-B_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T},
\]
are rational functions whose denominators are products of the strictly positive principal minors just identified.  Thus the denominator-clearing operation in \(\text{def:pairwise-exceptional-variety}\) preserves whether each off-diagonal residual entry vanishes.

Fix \(1\le a<b\le m\) and \(\pi\ne\pi_0\).  Because two distinct total orders disagree on the orientation of some unordered pair, there are \(u,v\in V\) such that \(u\) precedes \(v\) under \(\pi_0\), while \(v\) precedes \(u\) under \(\pi\).  Consider \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\) from \(\text{def:wrong-order-nonvanishing-witness}\).  For \(w\in\{u,v\}\), simultaneous permutation of the view indices writes \(\Gamma_w\) as the direct sum of
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&r_w\\ r_w&1\end{pmatrix}
\quad\text{and}\quad I_{m-2}.
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(1-r_w\), \(1+r_w\), and \(1\) with multiplicity \(m-2\), all positive because \(r_w\in(-1,1)\).  Every other \(\Gamma_i\) equals \(I_m\), and the sole nonzero coefficient, \(B^{(a)}[v,u]=B^{(b)}[v,u]=\beta\), respects \(\pi_0\).  Hence \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), including when \(m=2\).

Coordinates outside \(\{u,v\}\) are uncorrelated with this two-coordinate subsystem in each view, so adjoining them to a predecessor set leaves the following population regression coefficients unchanged.  In each of views \(a\) and \(b\),
\[
X_u=\varepsilon_u,
\qquad
X_v=\beta\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_u)=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_v)=1.
\]
Since \(v\) precedes \(u\) under \(\pi\), the two wrong-order innovations furnished by \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) are
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_v=X_v,
\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon_u
=X_u-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X_u,X_v)}{\operatorname{Var}(X_v)}X_v
=X_u-\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}X_v.
\]
The cross-variable disturbance orthogonality built into \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\), together with the specified witness covariances, now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
\widetilde\varepsilon_u^{(a)},
\widetilde\varepsilon_v^{(b)}
\right)
&=
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
\frac{\varepsilon_u^{(a)}-\beta\varepsilon_v^{(a)}}{1+\beta^2},
\beta\varepsilon_u^{(b)}+\varepsilon_v^{(b)}
\right)\\
&=\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}(r_u-r_v)\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is an off-diagonal entry of \(R_\pi^{ab}\), up to transpose orientation.  Since its denominator is positive, its cleared numerator is nonzero at \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\).  Thus every \(F_\pi^{ab}\) appearing in \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}\) is a nonzero polynomial.

There are finitely many unordered view pairs and wrong permutations.  The polynomial ring over \(\mathbb R\) in the finitely many free coordinates is an integral domain, so the finite product \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}\) of the nonzero factors is itself nonzero.  By \(\text{lem:nonzero-polynomial-null-set}\), its ambient zero set has Lebesgue measure zero and empty interior.  In the free-coordinate representation, \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is nonempty and open: it contains the point with every \(B^{(a)}=0\) and every \(\Gamma_i=I_m\), and the positive-definite cone is open.  Therefore the restriction of the zero set to \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), namely \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\), is proper and relatively Lebesgue null.  Any parameter law absolutely continuous with respect to relative Lebesgue measure assigns it probability zero by the definition of absolute continuity.

We next prove the exact failure-locus assertion.  Fix \(a<b\).  Because all denominators used in \(\text{def:pairwise-exceptional-variety}\) are positive,
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0
&\iff f_{\pi,ij}^{ab}(\theta)=0\quad\text{for every }i\ne j\\
&\iff \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab}(\theta))=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first equivalence follows because \(F_\pi^{ab}\) is a sum of real squares; the second is the positive denominator-clearing equivalence proved above.  Also
\[
R_\pi^{ba}=(R_\pi^{ab})^{\mathsf T}
\]
by \(\Sigma^{ba}=(\Sigma^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\), so one orientation tests the unordered pair.  The true order \(\pi_0\) is compatible by \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).  Applying that lemma and the definition of \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta\in\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}
&\iff F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0
   \quad\text{for at least one }\pi\ne\pi_0\\
&\iff \Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})\ne\{\pi_0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves equality of the exceptional set and the order-nonidentification locus.

If \(\theta\notin\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\), every factor in \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\theta)\) is nonzero.  The preceding equivalence, applied to every unordered pair and every wrong order, yields simultaneously
\[
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{\pi_0\}
\qquad(1\le a<b\le m).
\]
The complete coefficient characterization in \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) therefore gives
\[
\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\]
Full calibration retains the true order and imposes every pairwise restriction, so its compatible-order set is contained in the compatible-order set for any fixed pair.  Hence
\[
\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\]
Thus equality between the structural coefficient target and the observable residual-restriction functional has been derived rather than stipulated.

If \(\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})\ne\{T_{\pi_0}\}\), then its compatible-order set cannot equal \(\{\pi_0\}\).  The coefficient-nonidentification locus is consequently contained in \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\).  The containment can be strict.  Indeed, take every \(B^{(a)}=0\) and every \(\Gamma_i=I_m\).  Then \(\Sigma^{aa}=I_p\) and \(\Sigma^{ab}=0\) whenever \(a\ne b\).  For every \(\pi\), \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) gives \(B_\pi^{(a)}=0\), and \(R_\pi^{ab}=0\) for distinct views.  Therefore
\[
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\mathfrak S_V,
\qquad
\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{(0)_{a\in M}\}=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\]
Since \(p\ge2\), a wrong order exists, so this parameter lies in \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\) but not in the coefficient-nonidentification locus.

It remains to prove the lower half of the calibration frontier.  Fix arbitrary \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\) and \(a\in M\).  The rows of \(L_\pi^{(a)}X^{(a)}\) are the successive least-squares innovations from \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\).  The population normal equations make the innovation in position \(k\) orthogonal to every variable in positions \(1,\ldots,k-1\).  Each earlier innovation is a linear combination of those earlier variables.  Hence distinct innovations are orthogonal, and
\[
D_\pi^{(a)}:=R_\pi^{aa}
=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\]
is diagonal.  It is positive definite because \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\) and \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is invertible, so every \(D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]>0\).

For every \(j\in V\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\pi,j}^{\mathrm{marg}}
:=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\bigl(D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]\bigr)\succ0.
\]
To construct a full law explicitly, let \((Z_j)_{j\in V}\) be independent standard Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^m\), and set
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_j
:=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\!\left(\sqrt{D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]}\right)Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde X^{(a)}=(I_p-B_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde\varepsilon_j)=\Gamma_{\pi,j}^{\mathrm{marg}}\), and the coordinate disturbance stacks are independent across \(j\).  The resulting law is jointly centered Gaussian, has common order \(\pi\), satisfies cross-variable disturbance orthogonality, and has positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances.  Furthermore,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)})
=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}D_\pi^{(a)}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
=\Sigma^{aa},
\]
where the last equality is the displayed definition of \(D_\pi^{(a)}\) rearranged using invertibility of \(L_\pi^{(a)}\).  Thus every \(\pi\) has a full component-aligned completion of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{marg}}\).  Conversely, at fixed \(\pi\), the population normal equations and the invertibility of each predecessor covariance uniquely determine the order-constrained coefficients as those in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\).  Consequently
\[
\Pi_{\mathrm{marg}}=\mathfrak S_V,
\qquad
\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]

Now suppose \(\theta\notin\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\), and choose \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), possible because \(p\ge2\).  If \(T_\pi=T_{\pi_0}\), then \(L_\pi^{(a)}=L_{\pi_0}^{(a)}\) for every view \(a\).  Under the data-generating component-aligned representation,
\[
R_{\pi_0}^{ab}
=\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon^{(a)},\varepsilon^{(b)})
=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[a,b])
\]
is diagonal for every pair.  Equality of the residualizers would imply \(R_\pi^{ab}=R_{\pi_0}^{ab}\), and hence \(F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0\), for every \(a<b\).  This contradicts \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\theta)\ne0\).  Therefore \(T_\pi\ne T_{\pi_0}\), proving \(\lvert\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}\rvert\ge2\).

If \(\lvert C\rvert\le1\), no paired cross-view block is observed and, by definition, \(\Theta_C^{\mathrm{ext}}=\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}\ne\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\).  If \(\lvert C\rvert=2\), the simultaneous pair result gives \(\Theta_C^{\mathrm{ext}}=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\).  Hence
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{cal}}=2.
\]
The original definition of \(S_{\min}\) minimizes only over subsets of size at least two, and the same pairwise equality gives \(\lvert S_{\min}\rvert=2\).  Such a pair is a proper subset of \(M\) exactly when \(m\ge3\); when \(m=2\), it is all of \(M\).  Every step above used only the fixed-order component-aligned Gaussian parameter space and the displayed frozen definitions and lemmas.  In particular, no edge-minimality condition and no diversity condition from Assumption 2 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM was imposed.
